# `trim: true` follows JavaScript String.prototype.trim exactly: the trimmed
# set is ECMA-262 WhiteSpace + LineTerminator, which is NOT the same as the
# Unicode White_Space property Go's unicode.IsSpace tests. The two disagree in
# both directions, so both directions are pinned below.
# ZWNBSP / BOM (U+FEFF) IS trimmed by JS but is category Cf, so it is not
# Unicode White_Space. This is the ini `\ufeffa=1` BOM-in-the-first-key case.
<\ufeff hello \ufeff>
<\ufeffhello>
# Every other member of the set, leading and trailing at once.
# NEL (U+0085) is Unicode White_Space but is neither WhiteSpace nor
# LineTerminator in ECMA-262, so JS leaves it in place. A Go port that reached
# for unicode.IsSpace instead of the enumerated set fails exactly here.
# Neither is category-Cf padding: ZWSP and the Mongolian vowel separator.
<\u200bhello\u200b>
<\u180ehello\u180e>
# LF and TAB again, via the loader's own escapes rather than \uXXXX.
<\n\t hello \t\n>
# Trimming is an edge operation only: interior members survive untouched.
<  a\ufeff\u00a0b  >
# A block that is nothing but trimmable padding trims to the empty string.
<\ufeff \u3000>
